referee: referee 2 of 3 - the entropy walk's named attack surfaces, S8 as applied, iter-116 brackets
method: every constant re-derived from the definitions before comparison with the printed value; symbolic re-derivation and numerical cross-checks in referee2_check.py
main: No arithmetic defect. The iter-98 repair is correct as executed and all four printed constants are exact. Three text-level defects, one of which (S9-a's iter-98 sentence) currently prints a covering argument that does not cover. A strictly better constant is available and recommended.

items.subject: tensorization over the subgraph-indexed product; conditioning convention
findings: Convention is Ent(f) <= Sum_i E[Ent^{(i)}(f)] with Ent^{(i)} integrating coordinate i only, all others frozen - exactly the convention under which BLM 6.15 applies conditionally.
T_+ is a minimum over a fixed path set, not a law conditioned on an event; the half-plane therefore cannot break the product structure.

Localization re-derived: minimisers lie in the l1-ball of radius 2(b/a_w) r (a path reaching l1-distance R has >= 2R - r edges, time >= 4br - a_w r > br at R = 2(b/a_w) r), and the bound survives resampling since tau' <= b. The box is deterministic, so there is no random index set.
Ent^{(i)} = 0 outside the box; the count #G_+ and the tensorization sum use the same index set.

items.subject: intersection of ALL geodesics under non-uniqueness, in H; measurable selection
findings: The implication (T'-T)^+ > 0 => e in intersection-of-all-H-geodesics never uses uniqueness; non-uniqueness shrinks the intersection and can only help.

No measurable selection is needed anywhere: membership has the closed form e in G_+ <=> T_+^{avoid e} > T_+, a Borel set in the finite localized problem. C1 section 0's selection convention is compatible and idle.

H is strictly easier than the full plane: existence of a minimiser is by finiteness of the H-path set in the box (non-empty because the wall segment is an H-path), where the full-plane survey needs a genuinely random exponential-moment estimate.
S6 re-derived: (T'-T)^+ <= tau'_i <= b; the walk's use of tau'_i rather than the tighter (tau'_i - tau_i)^+ is required to keep independence from sigma(tau) for the decoupling step.

items.subject: constant chase as applied

constants_checked.E q(lambda tau') <= 2 lambda^2 b^2: CORRECT (sup q(x)/x^2 on (0,1] = e-1 = 1.71828; on the window actually used, x <= 1/2, it is 1.29744)
constants_checked.log E exp(#G_+/a0) <= (b/a_w) r/a0: CORRECT, deterministic from Claim 4 (#G_+ <= T_+/a_w <= br/a_w)
constants_checked.range t in (0, 4 b^2 sqrt(r)/a_w): CORRECT, reproduced symbolically; the two agree at the endpoint (both give exp(-br/a_w)), an independent consistency check

additional: The survey display Ent <= [aEq/(1-aEq)] log E exp(#G/a) E U was re-derived from entropy duality, so the walk no longer depends on the extraction's fidelity at p.49.

Sanity check on a degenerate toy (fixed path of m edges, weights on {1,2}, m=40): the entropy-method bound is never violated by the exact log-mgf, loose by ~64x - a too-small constant would have surfaced here.

improved_constant.statement: P(T_+ - E T_+ >= t sqrt(r)) <= exp(-a_w t^2/(8 b^3)) for t in (0, 4 b^2 sqrt(r)/a_w)
improved_constant.route: Claim 4 bounds #G_+ deterministically, so the variational step is unnecessary: Ent <= Eq . (b/a_w) r . E U = 2 lambda^2 b^3 (r/a_w) E U on the wider window lambda in (0, 1/b].
improved_constant.gain: exponent constant improved by a factor 2; identical t-range
improved_constant.structural_point: it deletes the parameter a whose mis-setting (a = r) was the original defect, so the mechanism of that bug leaves the architecture rather than merely being set to a safe value

items.subject: iter-116 overlap bracket and candidate instantiation
findings: Deterministic branch empties the event for r < (z/b)^2 (T_+ - E T_+ <= (b - a_w) r <= b r).
S8 branch admits t = z for r > (a_w z/(4 b^2))^2.
Overlap iff a_w < 4b, always true since a_w <= b; the threshold ratio is a_w^2/(16 b^2) <= 1/16, so the overlap is at least a factor-16 window in r, for every (a_w, b) and every z > 0.

Integer check the walk does not make and should: if (z/b)^2 <= 1 the deterministic branch covers no integer, but then z <= b and the S8 floor is <= 1/16 < 1, so S8 alone covers every integer r >= 1. Coverage of all integer r >= 1 at all z > 0 holds.
r* = z^2/(2 b^2) is admissible (needs a_w < 2 sqrt(2) b, weaker than a_w <= b).
NO smallness condition on delta is needed for coverage - the overlap condition contains neither z nor r.

Robust to either reading of C1's union: applying the tail at the common deviation z sqrt(R) instead of each pair's own r gives thresholds r > a_w z sqrt(R)/(4b^2) and r < z sqrt(R)/b, overlapping under the same condition a_w < 4b.

instantiation_match.C = 1: matches on both branches (deterministic branch contributes probability 0)
instantiation_match.strict vs non-strict event: C1 asks for the open event, the walk bounds the closed one - the stronger direction

items.distinction_to_keep: C1's union bound still needs delta > 0 STRICTLY so that exp(-c n^{2 delta}) beats the poly(n) pair count. That is a positivity requirement from C1's own counting (already implicit at C1 line 293), not a smallness requirement from the walk; the two must not be conflated.

items.subject: lower tail of T_+ non-consumption (walk asks its referee to confirm)
items.basis: independent enumeration of every probability statement in C1 (lines 84, 146, 157, 352, 364-365)
findings: Only two tails are consumed, both at line 146: free time LOWER (I2) and confined time UPPER (I3). No lower deviation of T_+ appears anywhere; line 364's probability is a geodesic-touching event, not a passage-time tail.

minor_defects.severity: minor, but it is a covering argument that does not cover
minor_defects.text: "for r <= r* the deterministic bound T_+ - E T_+ <= b r <= b r* empties the deviation event once z sqrt(r) > b r*"
minor_defects.problem: the condition is evaluated at the wrong r: for r <= r*, z sqrt(r) is smallest at small r, so 'z sqrt(r) > b r*' fails precisely on the part of the branch it must cover
minor_defects.fix: replace 'b r*' by 'b r' (equivalently, state the branch as r < (z/b)^2) or strike the clause - the iter-116 bracket two sentences later already states it correctly

minor_defects.problem: "INSIDE the restricted range with room to spare" is true only at the top scale r ~ n^kappa; at r = O(1) the deviation is far outside the Gaussian range and it is S9-a that carries the pair
minor_defects.fix: add 'at the top scale', or order S9-a after S9

minor_defects.problem: the q-linearisation's precondition lambda tau' <= 1 (i.e. lambda <= 1/b) is used but never stated; it is implied by the printed window so nothing is wrong, but it is the hypothesis that pins the window's shape

minor_defects.severity: not a defect - slack worth naming
minor_defects.problem: the deterministic ceiling is (b - a_w) r, not b r, since E T_+ >= a_w r; the true deterministic branch is r < (z/(b - a_w))^2 and the overlap margin is larger than claimed

ledger_recommendation: The walk's S8 and S9-a are deliverable as printed. (H-I3)'s candidate closure by the entropy route stands on the constants a_w/(16 b^3) and 4 b^2/a_w, and C1 section 3's iter-116 instantiation quotes them correctly. Recommended for v4: the improved constant a_w/(8 b^3) on the same range (which also removes the parameter that carried the original defect) and the three text fixes.
